newsitem.title: USA: Bankers Trust, Alex. Brown to merge.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust, Alex. Brown to merge.

text.p: U.S. banking company Bankers Trust New York Corp and retail brokerage firm Alex. Brown Inc said on Sunday they signed a definitive agreement to merge in a stock swap valued at about $1.7 billion.
Under terms of the deal, which was unanimously approved by both companies' boards, each Alex Brown common share would be exchanged for 0.83 shares of Bankers Trust common stock, the companies said.

"In a single, integrated firm, clients will have the benefit of Bankers Trust's expertise in syndicated bank lending and high-yield bonds and Alex. Brown's strength in equities research and underwriting," Bankers Trust Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Frank Newman said.
Based on the April 4 closing price of Bankers Trust and Alex. Brown's primary shares outstanding, the merger would have a value of about $1.7 billion, the companies said.
On that basis, Alex. Brown shareholders would own about 20 percent of Bankers Trust shares outstanding after completion of the merger, they said.

Bankers Trust said it expected to recognise a one-time charge of about $80 million at closing, for restructuring and related costs. The deal, set to close in the fourth quarter, was expected to be tax-free to shareholders and accounted for on a pooling-of-interests basis, it said.

The firm said it expected the combined company to achieve annualised expense savings of about $80 million resulting from the elimination of redundant operations within 12 months of the close. Bankers Trust declined to comment on which operations would be considered redundant.
The transaction was seen to be accretive to earnings per share in the second year after close, Bankers Trust said.
The firm declined to comment further on how much the deal would add to earnings.

"Bankers Trust and Alex. Brown believe the combined firm will generate significant additions in revenue from providing existing clients of the two firms with an expanded range of services and from the enhanced ability of the merged firms to attract new clients," the companies said in a statement.
Additions were expected in equity underwriting, trading and sales and in high yield finance, they said.

Revenue additions were also seen in risk management, mergers, acquisitions and advisory services, they said. The expanded range of private banking, brokerage and investment management capabilities was also a benefit, they said.

"We are extremely excited to be joining a firm whose capabilities support and extend our core strengths," A.B. Krongard, Alex. Brown chairman and chief executive said. "By combining the oldest investment banking firm in America with a premier global financial institution known for innovation, we are creating an exceptional organization ideally positioned to serve our clients."

Bankers Trust said its board intended to elect Krongard a director and vice chairman. Alex. Brown's headquarters would remain in Baltimore, the companies said. Mayo Shattuck III, Alex. Brown's president and chief operating officer, would also be named a vice chairman of Bankers Trust, it said.

Shattuck and Yves deBalmann, Bankers' co-head of investment banking and head of risk management services, would jointly lead the integration of the firms' investment banking business, the companies said.

At Bankers' recent board meeting, the firm said deBalmann, as well as Richard Daniel, chief financial officer, and R. Kelly Doherty, head of sales and trading and the firm's Latin American activities, were elected vice chairmen.

In connection with the deal, Alex. Brown granted Bankers Trust an option, exercisable under certain conditions, to acquire shares representing 19.9 percent of Alex. Brown's outstanding shares, the firm said.

Bankers Trust said it also granted Alex. Brown an option to buy up to 10 percent of Bankers Trust's outstanding stock, exercisable under certain conditions. The deal was subject to regulatory and shareholder approval, the companies said.
